biography.plain_text: Sir Thomas Sopwith was a British aviation pioneer and industrialist whose early aircraft businesses grew into Hawker Siddeley. Born into an engineering family, he inherited an income and began as a pilot and flying-school proprietor. His companies produced the Sopwith Camel and later helped shape the British military aircraft industry.

long_biography.plain_text:
Sir Thomas Sopwith brought aircraft technology into competitive sailing, equipping his America's Cup challengers with instruments to measure wind speed and direction. He organised the campaigns and took the helm himself. Before entering the contest, he had won England's Twelve-Metre championship four times in succession.

His first challenge in 1934 began with two victories, but the American defenders won the next four races. He returned in 1937 with a more advanced design, only to face the American defender Ranger. He was later inducted into the America's Cup Hall of Fame.
